To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a substantial proportion of respondents in a large cohort of adults reported sun-seeking behavior to increase endogenous Vitamin D levels; 2) sun-seeking was not related to a personal history of skin cancers; and 3) sun-seeking was associated with female gender, older age, lower education level, and Vitamin D supplement use.
30% of the respondents were aware of the health benefits of vitamin D, and of those, 42% said they went out into the sun in an attempt to increase vitamin D.

a substantial proportion of the public is aware of the benefits of sun exposure for increasing endogenous vitamin D and that some of them are sun-seeking to achieve these health benefits, which is a behavior that conflicts with the public health message of minimizing sun exposure to prevent skin cancer.
